title: Ratecap simulations & escalation checklist for QBRs
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a compact set of ratecap / token-spend simulation scenarios and a practical escalation checklist we can run before and during renewal QBRs. Goal is to give CSMs a repeatable recipe to: 1) quantify runway and overage risk, 2) recommend short-term mitigations (soft caps, burst policies), and 3) trigger the correct internal escalation when spend or traffic patterns threaten budgets or SLA targets.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: CSMs running renewal QBRs, FinOps support, Solutions Engineers (SEs) for technical remediation.
- Scope: Hosted API customers with metered token billing. Does NOT include Dedicated reserved-capacity customers (separate playbook).

How to use this doc (quick checklist):
- Pull the last 90 days of token usage and per-minute request counts (CS dashboard + Billing export).
- Compute baseline metrics (see worksheet below).
- Run the three scenarios (Normal growth, Burst/spike, Integration misconfig) and capture projected monthly spend and % overage.
- Decide recommendation: soft-ratecap, quota bump, schedule deep-dive.
- Notify internal stakeholders per escalation matrix.

Baseline worksheet (copy into your QBR notes):
Client: <customer-name>
Period: last 90 days (rolling)
- Avg tokens/day: 18,400
- Median tokens/hr (working hours): 750
- Peak tokens/hr (observed): 9,200
- Avg call size (tokens/request): 420
- Avg requests/sec (30-day): 4.3 req/s
- Monthly tokens (30-day projection): 552,000
- Current monthly committed tokens (if any): 500,000
- Current per-minute rate limit: 8,000 tokens/min (soft throttle)
- Current cost per 1k tokens: $0.45

Scenario A — Moderate growth (planning): +25% monthly tokens
- Projection: 552,000 * 1.25 = 690,000 tokens/month
- Extra tokens = 138,000 -> estimated extra cost = (138 * $0.45) = $62.1k (note: convert to same units; here units are 1k tokens so calculation: 138k/1k = 138 * 0.45 = $62.1)
- Risk: likely to hit billing alert threshold at +20% -> notify FinOps and discuss commit increase at renewal.
- Recommended short-term mitigation: enable prefix caching for high-frequency prompts, suggest 5–10% sampling of responses for eval to reduce token churn.

Scenario B — Short burst (integration bug, 3 hour window)
Assumptions: burst increases request rate 10x for 3 hours between 09:00–12:00 local
- Baseline tokens/hr (peak) = 9,200 -> burst tokens/hr = 92,000
- Burst tokens (3h) = 276,000 -> equivalent to ~50% of normal monthly tokens in 3 hours
- Immediate impact: If rate-limited by tokens/min (8k tokens/min), requests will get throttled and some retries will queue -> client experience/degradation.
- Suggested immediate actions:
  1) Apply temporary soft cap (global) for this client at consumption = 1.5x baseline peak to limit runaway cost.
  2) Contact SE to check telemetry and identify root cause (cron job, infinite loop, integration test left on).
  3) Escalate internally to SRE if burst correlates with backend anomalies (latency, errors rising).

Scenario C — Misconfigured SDK causing small requests to run in a loop (sustained 7 days)
- Symptoms: steady 2x baseline tokens/day for 7+ days, many small calls, high tail latency for their top routes.
- Projection: daily tokens *2 -> monthly tokens double -> immediate renewal conversation required.
- Recommended actions: throttle per-route, require client to fix SDK/loop, offer temporary credits if bug caused by our recent SDK change (investigate).

Escalation matrix (who to call in what order):
- Tier 0 (informational): +10–20% week-over-week increase or one-off day >2x baseline -> CSM notes in QBR prep, add to playbook, advise customer.
- Tier 1 (action): sustained +20–50% monthly projection OR burst event causing >10% of monthly tokens in <24h -> CSM + FinOps alerted (email + slack), open CS-incident ticket, propose short-term soft cap and schedule deep-dive.
- Tier 2 (urgent): sustained >50% projection OR 24h unmitigated burst OR possible security/abuse -> CSM, FinOps, SRE, SE all paged; apply temporary hard cap if necessary; prepare contingency commit offer for renewal.

Escalation contact templates (CS->FinOps Slack snippet):
"Heads-up — <customer> showing sustained +34% token growth vs 30d baseline, projected +$XXk next 30d. Proposing temporary soft cap at X tokens/min. Can FinOps advise on commit bump options? JIRA: CS-1214"

Ratecap policy recommendations to discuss in QBR:
- Soft cap vs hard cap: prefer soft caps (delayed 429s with warning headers) for first response.
- Burst window: recommend per-customer burst allowance = 3x median-hourly for up to 1 hour. Longer sustained bursts auto-escalate.
- Route-level caps: enable per-route tokens/min limits for high-cost endpoints (embedding vs generation).
- Alerts: set billing alerts at +10%, +25%, +50% thresholds with both email and slack.

QBR conversation checklist (CS preps):
- Bring baseline metrics and projections (copy worksheet).
- Show scenarios A-C with concrete dollars and % of committed tokens.
- Ask: Are we expecting new feature launches or data migrations? Any planned traffic?
- Propose 3 options: no-change, short-term soft cap + monitoring, commit increase (numbers + term recommendation).
- Decision capture: record the selected option and next steps.

Sample calculations (how to convert usage to $ quickly):
- monthly_tokens_k = monthly_tokens / 1000
- estimated_cost = monthly_tokens_k * unit_price_per_1k
Example: 690,000 tokens -> 690k/1k = 690 units -> 690 * $0.45 = $310.5

Meeting artifacts to attach to QBR doc:
- 90-day usage CSV export (billing)
- Per-route latency + quantiles (observability link)
- Top 10 prompts by tokens (helps find caching candidates)
- Any outstanding support tickets related to SDKs/integrations

Open questions / notes to self:
- Should we standardize a "3-tier offer" discount for mid-term commit bumps? (Marco to run pricing sensitivity)
- SEs: can you add a per-route cap toggle into the console by end of Q2? (JIRA: FE-889)
- Confirm whether function-calling high-volume customers should be billed differently (cost center check w/ Product).

Action items (next 7 days):
- CSM: attach baseline worksheet for all renewal QBRs this quarter (owner: Priya).
- FinOps: build an automated alert that computes projected 30d spend with linear extrapolation and posts to #cs-qbr-threads (owner: Evelyn).
- SE: create a checklist for prefix/response caching quick wins (owner: Jared).

Appendix: quick-template email to customer for pre-QBR token review:
"Hi <name>,
We pulled your last 90 days of usage and ran a short set of scenarios to help with the renewal conversation. Key takeaways: your month-to-date token run-rate projects to ~X tokens (Y% over your current commit). During the QBR wed like to review 3 mitigation options (no-change, soft cap + monitoring, commit bump). Please flag any upcoming product launches that might change traffic patterns.
Thanks,
Priya"

Revision history (brief):
- 2025-11-12 initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-12-04 added burst math and escalation matrix (Marco)
- 2026-02-28 updated sample calculations and linked artifacts (Evelyn)

End of doc.
